title: Analytics Stitcher: orchestrated schema evolution and SDK/CLI/API compatibility
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Build an "analytics stitcher" service that sits between ingestion and the analytics warehouse to orchestrate schema evolution across SDK/CLI/API sources. The stitcher will: 1) detect incoming event versions and apply deterministic, replayable transforms (grafts) to normalize events to the current analytics schema; 2) negotiate capabilities per-source (e.g., new fields, removed fields, lossy mappings) and record per-event provenance; 3) provide a staged migration orchestration to rollout schema changes gradually with canaries, automatic rollbacks on regression signals, and a backfill controller for historical data; 4) emit transformation logs and compact deltas for lineage and auditing.

We need this because our current approach of migrating producers in-place causes outages, inconsistent dashboards, and complex backfills. The stitcher enables compatibility-first rollouts and makes analytics consumers schema-stable while producers evolve independently. This ticket covers design, a lightweight prototype sidecar, feature gates for per-tenant negotiation, and an initial production rollout plan for two high-volume event families (inference.requests, console.interaction).
comments: 2025-11-12 - Kickoff: scoped MVP to support two event families, graft operations limited to field rename + type coercion + field drop with lossy-policy tagging. Action: prototype sidecar in telemetry-injector. -- Maya

2025-11-28 - Architecture review with infra. Decided to implement stitcher as stateful stream processor with idempotent apply semantics rather than mutating producers. Trade-offs: adds processing latency (~3-8ms p95) but avoids producer changes. -- Ravi

2025-12-10 - Design feedback from Olivia Park (PM): require explicit canary cohorts, and expose a migration dashboard. Add metrics: transform_success_rate, transform_latency_ms, transform_rejection_count. -- Olivia
2026-01-05 - Security review request submitted; infra flagged KMS access for provenance signing. Logged in security queue (SEC-2026-09).

2026-01-22 - Prototype PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/2436. Prototype includes in-memory graft engine and YAML-based transform rules. Requesting initial code review. -- Ravi

2026-02-02 - Review notes from Diego Alvarez (Design): request sample visualizations for rollback windows. Also recommended adding a synthetic prompt set to validate semantic integrity after transforms. -- Diego

2026-02-15 - Canary run started for 10% of dev-tenant traffic. Early metric: transform_success_rate=99.97%, downstream dashboard delta within noise. Observed 0.5% increase in event processing cost; acceptable for initial rollout. -- Maya

2026-02-20 - Blocker: observed edge case with deeply nested JSON arrays causing failure in graft rule engine. Current mitigation: fallback to 'pass-through with provenance' and raise transform_rejection_count. Task created to add array-path flattening rule.
acceptance_criteria: Stitcher prototype deployed to staging processing inference.requests and console.interaction with deterministic graft rules
Transform logs emitted to analytics_events_transform_log topic and retained for 90 days
Canary orchestration supports cohort definition, automatic rollback on regression signal, and manual promotion
Backfill controller can run incremental replays for a configured time window and annotate events with provenance metadata
SDK/CLI/API clients continue to operate without code changes during the staged rollout (compatibility validated)
Runbook and dashboard pages created: migration dashboard, transform failure dashboard, cost impact dashboard
steps: Design: finalize graft rule DSL and lossy-field-mapping policy (owner: Maya)
Implement: lightweight graft engine library with idempotent replayable semantics (owner: Ravi)
Infra: deploy stitcher as a stateful stream processor cluster (owner: SRE)
Integrations: add per-tenant capability negotiation API for SDK/CLI to advertise supported fields (owner: SDK team)
Observability: emit metrics and trace hooks; wire transform logs to analytics_events_transform_log (owner: Observability)
Canary: run cohorted rollout, collect regression signals (owner: PM + SRE)
Backfill: implement incremental backfill controller and test on a small historical window (owner: Data Eng)
